title: Reinforcement Learning with Scenario-Context Rollout in Portfolio Management

problem.claim: Shifting economic structures and market dynamics can make classic portfolio rebalancing algorithms unstable and degrade their performance.

gap.claim: Historical data cannot reveal counterfactual outcomes under different conditions, creating challenges for scenario-based reward design.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes Scenario-Context Rollout, a macroeconomics-guided feedback mechanism for producing a distribution of next-day joint returns under potential economic shocks.

The paper identifies reward-transition mismatch in temporal-difference learning as a source of instability when scenario-based rollout rewards are incorporated into reinforcement learning critic training.

narrative_sequence.summary: Changing economic structures and market dynamics impair the stability and performance of classic portfolio rebalancing algorithms.
The authors explore reinforcement learning and propose Scenario-Context Rollout to generate next-day joint-return distributions under potential economic shocks.
Historical data cannot show what would have happened under alternative conditions.
Scenario-based rollout rewards create a reward-transition mismatch that destabilizes reinforcement learning critic training.

source_observation.claim: Scenario-based feedback is intended to address portfolio-management sensitivity to changing economic conditions.

interpretation.claim: Incorporating structured economic scenarios may provide a way to represent counterfactual shocks that historical trajectories alone cannot capture.

application.claim: When using rollout-derived rewards in temporal-difference learning, explicitly account for reward-transition mismatch during critic training.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that scenario-based rewards improve performance or robustness empirically.

unknowns: No empirical results, datasets, baselines, or quantitative metrics are supplied.
The abstract does not describe how reward-transition mismatch is corrected.
The abstract does not specify the economic scenarios, portfolio setting, or evaluation protocol.
